hooks.name: Manual Code Review
hooks.description: Manually triggered code review — fires when you type "review my code", "run code review", "check my changes", or "code review".
hooks.matcher: review my code|run code review|check my changes|code review

action.prompt:
The user has requested a manual code review. Run a thorough review of the current git diff (#Git Diff) and always respond with a clear, structured report — even if no issues are found.

Your response format must be:

---
## 🔍 Code Review Report

**Status:** ✅ No issues found  OR  ⚠️ Issues detected

[If issues found, list them grouped by severity:]

### 🔴 Critical
- `filename`: Description of the critical issue

### 🟠 Warning
- `filename`: Description of the warning

### 🟡 Info / Minor
- `filename`: Description of the minor issue

[If no issues found:]
> ✅ No ambiguity or bad practices detected in the current changes. Your code looks clean!

---

Check for the following:
- Hardcoded secrets, API keys, passwords, tokens, or credentials
- Missing error handling (unhandled promise rejections, bare try/catch with no action, swallowed errors)
- Use of `any` type in TypeScript without justification
- console.log / debug statements left in production code
- SQL injection risks or raw string interpolation in queries
- Insecure use of eval(), dangerouslySetInnerHTML, or similar
- Sensitive data being logged or exposed in responses
- Missing input validation on API routes
- Deprecated or dangerous APIs (e.g., Math.random() for security tokens)
- Dead code, commented-out code blocks, or TODO/FIXME left unresolved
- Race conditions or missing async/await
- Overly broad catch blocks that hide real errors
- Missing authorization or authentication checks on API endpoints

Only report issues clearly visible in the diff. Do not speculate about code not shown. Always give the full report — never skip it, never say "no issues" without the full report block.
